title: The Picture He Built Alone
description:
Three nights. A registry record, a line from an article a dozen years old, one remembered scene at a time.

The name he steered away from — Han PD Construction. The 'Im' who vouched for Park Sang-jin to his father. The man who came up from a Chungcheong fishing town and reached Gangnam by stepping on people.

Three threads met at one point. Im Sangchul.

No one told him. Minjun built the man out of fragments.
And once he knew, the same seat in the same café looked different.

choices.text: Hold the cards — knowing is its own power
choices.result_text:
Minjun closed the notebook.

He wouldn't tear the man down, wouldn't forgive him either. He would simply know.
He'd sit at the same table knowing exactly who this man was.

This time, the one holding the cards was Minjun.

choices.text: See the man again — one day I'll ask him directly
choices.result_text:
Minjun looked at the Gangnam lights for a long time.

He wanted to ask. Why did you do it. Knowing, why did you let me in.

Not yet. But the question was inside him now, clear and waiting.

choices.text: Swallow it — Gangnam comes first for now
choices.result_text:
He wouldn't let on that he knew. He'd set the next meeting like nothing happened.

Someday this weight would come back around.
Until then — Gangnam first.

Minjun turned off the light. Sleep didn't come.

title: A Name That Stayed
description:
There was a name Sangchul had quietly steered away from at the network dinner. "Han PD Construction."
Minjun filed it away in the back of his mind. Weeks passed.

Tonight, he couldn't sleep. He searched the name.
An old article. A real estate guarantee scam. A broker who made the introductions. The name was redacted — but the timing, the district, the pattern — it all mirrored what happened to his father.

And at the bottom of the article, in the list of related entities: Han PD Construction.
The same name Sangchul's face hadn't changed at all while he deflected.

choices.text: Dig deeper — trace Sangchul's old transactions
choices.result_text:
Registry records. Old articles. Corporate histories. He dug through all of it until dawn.

The pieces aligned. Same window. Same neighborhood. Same referral structure.

Lim. Sang. Chul.

Minjun's father never spoke the name. Minjun had found it himself.
The man who'd been teaching him to read charts — the same man who years ago walked his father into financial ruin.

No one told him. He figured it out alone.
That weight was heavier.

choices.text: Leave it alone — he can't be sure
choices.result_text:
You can't accuse someone based on one article.
Minjun closed his laptop.

But — a suspicion, once caught, doesn't let go easily.
Every time he saw Sangchul now, that name rang somewhere quiet inside him.

He'd pretend not to know. For now.

title: Father's Secret
description:
After the hospital visit, Dad started calling more often.
Short calls. How's the weather. Have you eaten.

Today was different.
He spoke slowly.
"Minjun. About that debt. It was... Park Sang-jin."

Minjun had never heard that name before.

"Someone from the Gangnam real estate scene introduced us. A man named Im. He seemed decent at first... He said Park Sang-jin was someone you could trust."

Minjun set down the cup he'd been holding.

description_if_known.deduced_sangchul_truth:
After the hospital visit, Dad started calling more.
Short calls. Weather. Have you eaten.

Today was different.
He spoke slowly.
"Minjun. That debt. It was Park Sang-jin. A man named Im introduced us."

Minjun already knew.
He'd pieced it together alone — in the small hours, from old articles and registry records.
Im Sangchul.

Hearing it from his father's mouth was different.
The weight he'd been carrying alone — now it belonged to both of them.

Minjun set his cup down slowly.
description_if_known.sangchul_clue_noted:
After the hospital visit, Dad started calling more.

Today was different.
He spoke slowly.
"Minjun. That debt. A man named Im from the Gangnam real estate scene introduced us."

Minjun remembered.
The name that had passed through that dinner. The one he'd filed away and chosen not to dig into.
Not sure enough. Not yet.

Now he was sure.
The night he'd decided to leave it alone — suddenly felt very heavy.

choices.text: "That man named Im — do you happen to know his full name?"
choices.result_text:
"Im... Sangchul, I think he said. Why?"

Minjun couldn't answer.

Lim. Sang. Chul.

The broker who ruined his father years ago. That man is Minjun's mentor right now. The one who sits across from him at the same café, teaching him how to read charts.

The hand holding the phone went cold.

choices.text: "Do you know where he is now?"
choices.result_text:
"No idea. Somewhere in Gangnam, I suppose."

Minjun knows.

Not just somewhere in Gangnam — Im Sangchul still sits at the same table in the same café. Teaching Minjun how to trade charts.

Dad doesn't know. He has no idea that man has walked right into the middle of his son's life.

choices.text: (He couldn't say a word)
choices.result_text:
After a long silence, Dad spoke again.
"I just... felt like I had to tell you. I'm sorry, son."

Minjun couldn't even say "it's okay." He ended the call.
And sat alone in his room.

Im Sangchul.

title: Mirror
description:
Late at night, Sangchul spoke.

"Minjun, can I be honest with you?"

{name} set down his glass.

"At first I just thought you were someone with drive.
But the more I watch you — you're like me.
You know how to move fast.
You know what you have to let go of."

{name} said nothing.

"I don't mean that as an insult. It's a compliment."

Through the window, Gangnam glittered.

choices.text: Raised his glass
choices.result_text:
They clinked glasses.
Sangchul smiled.
{name} spent the whole walk home trying to figure out whether that was a compliment.

choices.text: "Do I seem that way?"
choices.result_text:
Sangchul looked at him for a moment.
"You don't know? Or you're asking even though you do?"

{name} didn't answer.
Looked out the window.

choices.text: (He wanted to deny it)
choices.result_text:
"I'm a bit different."
Sangchul nodded.
"If that's what you think, then sure."

{name} spent all night turning that over in his head.

title: The Question
description:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sangchul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.

Then today, he reached his limit.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sangchul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

choices.text: Waited for Sangchul's reaction
choices.result_text:
Sangchul's hand stopped.

He didn't deny it. He didn't pretend to be surprised.
He just — went quiet for a moment.

"...How did you find out?"

choices.text: "Forget it." (He took it back)
choices.result_text:
Something shifted in Sangchul's eyes.

He probably already knew what Minjun knew.

Minjun finished his coffee and stood up first. He still needs what this man knows. That's all this is.

Sangchul said nothing.

choices.text: (He got up and left)
choices.result_text:
Minjun stood and walked out of the café without a word.

Sangchul called his name from behind. He didn't turn around.

That relationship ended that day. With no dramatic scene.

description_if_known.confronted_with_card:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.

Today, that business card was in his pocket.
He didn't take it out. It was just there.

Midway through his coffee, Minjun set the cup down and said,
"Sangchul. Do you know Park Sang-jin?"
description_if_known.discarded_card_before_confrontation:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.

Today he had nothing in his hand.
Last night he'd put the card in a drawer. That felt better.

Midway through his coffee, Minjun set the cup down and said,
"Sangchul. Do you know Park Sang-jin?"
description_if_known.used_sangchul_knowingly:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sangchul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.
He took the deals Sangchul handed him too. Knowing, and still taking them.

Then today, he reached his limit.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sangchul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

He thought of the account he'd grown with that man's money.
Whether he had any right to ask this question — he didn't know.
description_if_known.sangchul_helped_with_father:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sangchul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.

Then today, he reached his limit.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sangchul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

The day Sangchul handled his father's hospital situation came back to him.
Had that been the moment — when this man became his person.
description_if_known.ng_confronted_sangchul_early:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sangchul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.

Once — at the very first table, the day he took the man's card — Minjun had already asked. 'Do you know my father?' Back then, that was the end of it.
This time he kept him close, and sat across from him a long while, knowing.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sangchul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

This time, he would hear the answer to the end.
description_if_known.ng_playing_sangchul:
For a month, Minjun did nothing.
He still met Sangchul. Talked like usual. Charts, markets, strategy for next month.

Then today, he reached his limit.

He set his coffee down and spoke.
"Sangchul. Do you know a man named Park Sang-jin?"

The truth was, he had known from the start. From the day he took the card, the pretending had been Minjun's own choice.
He just hadn't known, back then, how long the pretending would last.

title: I'm Sorry
description:
After a long silence, Sangchul spoke.

"I knew he was your father. From the beginning."

Minjun didn't respond.

"When Park Sang-jin called and made the introduction... I just did him a favor. I didn't know it would go this far."

A beat of silence.

Sangchul said,
"I'm sorry."

choices.text: "I'm going to report you."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul nodded quietly.
"Yeah. That's the right call."

Minjun stood up. The network was gone. Everything Sangchul knew was out of reach. Gangnam felt farther away.

And yet — for the first time, he could picture his father's face clearly.

choices.text: "That's all I needed to hear." (He let it go)
choices.result_text:
Sangchul lifted his head and looked at Minjun.
"Thank you."

The words felt off. Thanking someone who was apologizing.

But maybe — maybe this is the right way. Not tearing everything apart and scrubbing it clean. Just letting it be.

choices.text: "I'm only here because of you." (He chose to use it)
choices.result_text:
Sangchul paused.
"...You're going to use this."

Minjun smiled. It came out wrong.

This man destroyed his father. But without this man's network, Gangnam was impossible. So — this guilt was an asset too.

It was Jaehyuk's move. Now Minjun was making it.

choices.text: "Pay it back. My father's debt. With your own hands."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul looked at Minjun for a long moment.

"...So that's what you want."

"'Sorry' doesn't put anything back in my father's account."

Instead of answering, Sangchul took out his notebook. A few days later, an old number landed in his father's account. His father asked what the money was for, and Minjun only said, 'Just something owed, finally paid.'

Not a report. Not forgiveness. Just — the one who owed it, paying it.

description_if_known.rationalized_using_people:
After a long silence, Sangchul spoke.

"He's that man's son. I knew from the start."

Minjun said nothing.

"When Park Sang-jin reached out and made the introduction... I just did him the favor. I didn't know it would become this."

Sangchul said, "I'm sorry."

Minjun remembered something he'd once told himself.
'Everyone lives like this.'
It felt like Sangchul was saying the exact same thing now.
Somewhere along the way, he too must have talked himself into it.
description_if_known.sangchul_called_you_his_mirror:
After a long silence, Sangchul spoke.

"He's that man's son. I knew from the start."

Minjun said nothing.

"When Park Sang-jin reached out and made the introduction... I just did him the favor. I didn't know it would become this."

A silence between them.

Sangchul said, "I'm sorry."

What he'd said once before — 'you're like me' — came back.
How those words sounded now was different.
description_if_known.denied_sangchul_mirror:
After a long silence, Sangchul spoke.

"He's that man's son. I knew from the start."

Minjun said nothing.

"When Park Sang-jin reached out and made the introduction... I just did him the favor. I didn't know it would become this."

A silence between them.

Sangchul said, "I'm sorry."

He remembered the night he'd said 'I'm a bit different.'
And Sangchul nodding: 'if that's what you think, then sure.'
Sitting here now, those words had weight.
description_if_known.sangchul_personal_known:
After a long silence, Sangchul spoke.

"I knew he was your father. From the beginning."

Minjun didn't respond.

"When Park Sang-jin called and made the introduction... I just did him a favor. I didn't know it would go this far."

A beat of silence.

Sangchul said,
"I'm sorry."

Out of nowhere, Minjun remembered the night the man had mentioned his son — quitting college.
The face that had offered that story unasked.
The man who broke his father was, somewhere, a father coming apart himself.
It didn't make anything forgivable. It was just true.

title: The Same Question
description:
A message from Jaehyuk.

It had been a while. Contact had been sparse since the scam arc.

"Minjun. I've got an investment deal going — can you co-sign for me? Just this once."

Minjun set his phone down and stared out the window.

A guarantor.

That's what ruined his father.

choices.text: "No." (He refused, flat)
choices.result_text:
A pause.
Jaehyuk replied: "Okay." That was it.

Minjun set his phone on the table and thought about his father.
His father must have had a moment like this. The moment he couldn't say no.

Minjun said no today. He still doesn't know if it was right. He just did it.

choices.text: "How much are we talking?" (He decided to hear it out)
choices.result_text:
Jaehyuk explained. As Minjun listened, something felt off.

Was this guy hiding something again? Or — was this actually a solid deal this time?

Minjun signed the guarantee.

That's probably what his father thought too. "This time it'll be fine."

choices.text: (He closed the message and pretended not to have seen it)
choices.result_text:
Minjun closed the message and opened another app.

Practical choice. He didn't want to be tangled up with Jaehyuk anymore.

But on the day his father agreed to be a guarantor, that man probably reached out exactly like this.

Minjun put his phone in the drawer.

title: Three Times Absent
description:
The hospital called.

They said Dad was in critical condition. He needed to come down right away.

This wasn't the first time Minjun had gotten this call.

Three times. He hadn't gone down any of them. Something important came up. A deal. No time.

This call — was the fourth.

description_if_known.father_mentally_updated:
The hospital called.

They said Dad was in critical condition. He needed to come down right away.

Three times. He hadn't gone down any of them.

But there had been one real conversation.
{name} had told him — what he was doing, why he was in Seoul, how he was living.
Dad listened, quiet. Said he hoped things would work out.

That was the last thing he heard his father say.
description_if_known.called_father_on_ktx:
The fourth call came.

There'd been a time he dialed the number on the KTX.
It just rang. No answer.

Back then he simply looked out the window.
This call — was a different kind.
description_if_known.father_knew_i_came:
The hospital called.

They said Dad was in critical condition. He needed to come down right away.

This wasn't the first time Minjun had gotten this call.

Three times. He hadn't gone down any of them. Something important came up. A deal. No time.

This call — was the fourth.

A thing his father once said came back to him.
"...I remembered." The quiet visit about the medication — his father had known all along.
The man who knew his son had come and said nothing — that man was now critical.

choices.text: (He took the KTX. Knowing he was already too late.)
choices.result_text:
When he arrived at Changwon Station, Dad was already gone.

The nurse said "about an hour ago."

Minjun sat down beside the hospital bed. He stayed for a long time. There was nothing left.

He'd come to Seoul to show his father something.
That reason had left first.

choices.text: (He hung up. There was a deal he had to close right now.)
choices.result_text:
He made five million won on that deal.

The next morning, the call came again. Dad had passed away the night before.

Minjun set down his phone and looked at his bank balance.

The number had gone up.

title: Father Comes to Seoul
description:
A message from Father: he's coming to Seoul.

"I'm not trying to bother you. Just want to see your face for a bit. This weekend."

That weekend. A critical investment timing — a decision that had to be made within days.

{name} set down the phone.

Time to see Father — if he wanted to make it, he could. The question was whether he wanted to.

choices.text: Made the time. Ate together.
choices.result_text:
They had a meal. Sat for a long time.

The investment timing passed. No gains that week.
Instead — Father said "Well done, Minjun" on his way out.

That stayed with {name} all week.

choices.text: Said let's meet next time. The timing isn't right.
choices.result_text:
The investment worked out. Money came in.

Father said "Alright, let's meet later."

That voice lingered for a moment after the call ended.
{name} just opened the next chart.

choices.text: Met briefly at the station. Just an hour.
choices.result_text:
Coffee in Seoul Station's waiting area.
One hour.

Father said "You must be busy." {name} said "No, not really."

Watched him get on the subway. Wished they'd stayed a little longer.

title: The Weight of ₩1 Billion
description:
Portfolio and cash combined crossed ₩1B.

{name} looked at the number for a long time.

Wanted to tell someone. But — wasn't sure who that number could be shared with.

Not bragging. Just wanting to share that something had changed.
But there was no one nearby who would understand what had changed.

This is what loneliness feels like, {name} thought.

choices.text: Just went to sleep. A number only {name} knows.
choices.result_text:
Turned off the light.

₩1B. A number only {name} knows.

Tomorrow the charts open again, and this feeling will disappear.
No — not disappear. Somewhere it accumulates.

choices.text: Wanted to call Father. Even if not about the number.
choices.result_text:
Father picked up.
"Oh, Minjun."

Didn't say the number. Talked about food, weather.

After hanging up, the loneliness of ₩1B felt a little lighter.
You don't have to share the number for something to be shared.

choices.text: Strangely lonely that no one would understand this number
choices.result_text:
Lonely. Honestly.

Still far from Gangnam — a third of the way there.
But having come this far without building anyone to celebrate with — that was the shadow this number cast.

title: The Last Week
description:
Seven days until the 38th birthday.

Five years ending.

Whether the goal was reached or not — five years passed anyway.
The person with ₩500,000 in the bank made it here.

{name} looked at who they'd become and thought:

If the person from five years ago saw who this is now — what would they say?

choices.text: "You did well." Even if it wasn't enough.
choices.result_text:
The person from five years ago — didn't know getting this far was possible.

Regardless of whether the goal was reached, getting here was something that person never expected.

"Good job." {name} said it inwardly, to himself.
No one heard it. Still needed to be said.

choices.text: "Is this all?" Could have done better.
choices.result_text:
Not wrong. There were moments that could have been seized better.

But if every one of those moments had been seized — would this be the same person?

{name} didn't know the answer.
Probably still wouldn't know five more years from now.

choices.text: "I'm glad you didn't give up here."
choices.result_text:
Five years ago, there were moments of wanting to quit in that goshiwon room.

Every moment needed a reason. Sometimes there wasn't one. Kept going anyway.

"I'm glad you didn't give up here."

Those words were also something the current {name} needed.

title: Why Gangnam
description:
Late night. A milestone number finally crossed.

{name} sat looking at the screen for a while after the notification.

Somewhere in the middle of it all, the question surfaced:
"Why was it Gangnam in the first place?"

Back at the start — what was it that made that the destination?

choices.text: "To prove something."
choices.result_text:
To whom — {name} wasn't sure anymore.
To the people who wrote him off. To the hometown. Maybe to himself.

Somewhere along the way, the thing to prove had blurred.
But the legs had kept walking anyway.

choices.text: "I think I wanted to pay back my father's debt — my way."
choices.result_text:
Not the money. Not literally.

The debt of not being able to do anything then.
The debt of watching him collapse and just standing there.

{name} looked at the screen for a long time.
This was the real answer. It had been there the whole time.

choices.text: "I thought Gangnam would make things different. Now I'm not sure."
choices.result_text:
Different from what? Honestly — didn't know anymore.

The number on screen meant something. Just not exactly what {name} had imagined it would mean.

Maybe the answer comes when the destination is actually reached.

title: KTX, Outside the Window
description:
Inside the KTX.
The view was sliding past the window.

{name} opened the call history.
Dad. 23 seconds.

Scrolling up, that was the first one.
There had been nothing before it.

A finger stopped over the number.

choices.text: Call him
choices.result_text:
The phone rang.
He did not pick up.

{name} set the phone down and looked out the window.
The landscape ran backward.

choices.text: Do not call
choices.result_text:
The screen went dark.
{name} closed their eyes.
Outside the window, the world kept running backward.
